Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency follow-up / Redwood rate limits

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to see your traffic shape. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we have alignment before we draft a quota proposal:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: user-facing Q&A and short-form summarization inside your product.
- Latency target: p95 around 300ms for short prompts (~<128 tokens), p50 closer to 120–150ms.
- Throughput: expected sustained average ~200–250 req/s during business hours, occasional spikes.
- Concurrency: want to support ~80 parallel requests from a single region; ability to burst to ~150 for short windows.
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for perceived latency on the client.

Action items / next steps
1) Can you send a lightweight traffic sample (timestamps + tokens per request) — Jorge said he would share an export.
2) We'll prepare a recommended SLO/quota configuration and two pricing options: hosted quota increase vs Dedicated reserved capacity.
3) If we align on numbers, we'll scope a short pilot (2–4 weeks) to validate cold-starts, KV cache benefits, and sustained cost.

Attachments: acme-traffic-profile.csv (Jorge, if you can share the CSV from your app logs that will speed validation).

Thanks — I'll loop Rafael and Monica on the proposal side.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency follow-up / Redwood rate limits

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Attached is a small anonymized traffic sample (acme-traffic-profile.csv). A few clarifications from our engineering team: 

- Latency targets: p95 <= 300ms for prompt sizes up to 128 tokens. For longer prompts (<512 tokens) we can accept p95 <= 700ms.
- Throughput: sustained 220 req/s average, expected 30% headroom for growth in Q1.
- Concurrency model: each user request opens a connection and we expect up to 80 parallel active requests. We also use HTTP/2 connection pooling from our app servers; typical keep-alive settings hold 8 streams per connection.
- Streaming: yes — partial tokens should be delivered as generated. We rely on SSE/Websockets fallback when streaming latencies impact UX.
- Failover: If latency spikes we can tolerate a degraded model fallback (lower-cost model) for up to 2% of requests during incidents.

Attachment: acme-traffic-profile.csv (see column 'tokens' and 'timestamp' for distribution).

Let us know if you need anything else. Jorge, flag anything I missed.

—
Taylor Reed
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency follow-up / Redwood rate limits

Perfect, thanks for the sample. I pulled out the high-level numbers and sketched an SLO matrix (attached: SLO_matrix.xlsx) so we can discuss concrete quota options. Two points we want to confirm for the proposal: 

1) Target concurrency to propose: do you want us to price/configure for 80 sustained concurrent active requests with a configured burst to 150 for 5–10 minute windows?
2) Streaming expectations: we'll ensure streaming is enabled for the route; need to confirm whether you prefer SSE (our hosted API supports streaming SSE + HTTP/2 chunking) or a websocket-based approach on your side.

For pricing and quota options we'll include:
- Hosted increase: raise hosted account concurrency and token throughput limits (short lead time, soft quota)
- Dedicated reserved pool: dedicated GPU pool to guarantee concurrency, lower per-token cost, stronger SLOs and SLA-backed latency targets

If you're comfortable with the numbers above I'll draft a two-option proposal with estimated monthly cost and a recommended pilot configuration.

Attachments: SLO_matrix.xlsx

—
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Concurrency follow-up / Redwood rate limits

Thanks — good thread. A few notes on Redwood defaults and a proposed configuration for Acme: 

Redwood hosted default limits (typical):
- Concurrency (parallel requests): 60 active requests per account by default
- Burst capacity: short bursts up to 120 handled opportunistically (not SLA-backed)
- Token throughput: soft throttles applied per-minute; token/sec throttles vary by model family
- Streaming: supported; consistent with SSE/chunked HTTP streaming

Proposed configuration for Acme (two options):
A) Hosted quota increase (fastest to enable)
- Increase concurrency to 80 sustained, burst to 150 for 10-minute windows
- Raise token throughput ceilings consistent with your traffic profile
- Implement per-route connection pooling guidance (keep-alive, HTTP/2 streams)
- Price impact: ~+35% over current hosted usage spend (ballpark; will refine)

B) Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended if you want SLA-backed latency and predictable pricing)
- Dedicated pool sized to keep p95 <= 300ms for <128 tokens and handle sustained 250 req/s
- Guaranteed concurrency of 200 (headroom for future growth), with configurable per-route quotas
- Includes observability and tracing access, custom autoscaling policy
- Price impact: higher upfront commit but lower per-token unit cost; pilot pricing attached in offer doc

Operational notes:
- We can support HTTP/2 keep-alive and recommend 8–16 concurrent streams per connection from your app servers to reduce connection churn.
- For streaming, SSE is simplest on hosted; for websocket-based integrations we can provide proxy guidance.
- If you need automatic fallback to a cheaper model on overload, we can set route-level fallbacks and percent-based degradation rules.

Next steps we propose:
1) Marissa to send the two-option pricing draft + pilot scope.
2) If Acme prefers Hosted increase, we can provision a soft quota boost in 2–3 business days.
3) If Acme prefers Dedicated, we'll draft a pilot SOW (2–4 weeks) and a capacity sizing worksheet.

Looping in Lauren to coordinate CS/pilot enablement and ensure we have the right infra contacts.

—
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
